history.period: 9th-10th century CE context (sub-shrine; no separate dated inscription documented)
history.summary: IDENTITY FLAG: the 'Kashi Vishweshwara Swamy Shrine' of Draksharamam appears to be a subsidiary shrine inside the Sri Bhimeswara Swamy temple complex - described as the south-facing Kashi Vishweshwara shrine on the right side of the Bheemeswara temple and as the Visweswara Lingam among the small shrines along the mandapam corridor - not an independent temple. One local gazetteer-style account attributes a 'kashi viswesara temple' to Vyasa and mentions an Agastyeswara shrine worshipped by sage Agastya. No separate establishment date, administration or web footprint exists for it; it shares the history, district and coordinates of seq 1207.

name: Kashi Vishweshwara Swamy Shrine
town_description: Draksharamam (also Daksharamam) is an ancient temple town in Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district, about 28 km from Kakinada, 60 km from Rajahmundry and 6 km from Ramachandrapuram on the Rajahmundry-Yanam route. Known as Dakshina Kashi, it is a twin Shaiva-Shakti centre (Pancharama + Shakti Peetha) that draws pilgrims year-round, especially on Shivaratri.

travel.airport: Rajahmundry Airport (~55-60 km) is the nearest; Visakhapatnam is farther (verify distances).
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station Rajahmundry (RJY, ~60 km, verify); Ramachandrapuram (~6 km) is the nearest town.
travel.road: Inside the Bhimeswara temple complex on the Rajahmundry-Yanam road; same access as the main temple.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; follows the main temple calendar.
